findings.highlight: On an early morning like this, when normally only the sound of the newspaper delivery bike can be heard,
findings.evidenceJa: 雪菜の、まるで一曲ノーミスで弾ききったような歓声が響く。
findings.explanation: The sentence ends after establishing the otherwise silent dawn and omits its predicate: Setsuna's cheer rings out as if she has just played an entire song without one mistake. The missing musical simile is the joke that Haruki immediately deflates by noting that they only finished packing.
findings.japanese:
そんな、新聞配達員のバイク音以外は聞こえることのない
早朝に、雪菜の、まるで一曲ノーミスで弾ききったような
歓声が響く。
findings.todokanai: On an early morning like this, when normally only the sound of the newspaper delivery bike can be heard,

findings.highlight: Then on Wednesday we were tied down all day at work, and on Thursday we were forced to participate in a hot pot party,
findings.evidenceJa: 二日分の作業が停滞した。
findings.explanation: The line is left hanging after the two interruptions and omits their consequence: two full days of moving work stalled. That missing tally explains why the couple is still packing at six in the morning.
findings.japanese:
なのに水曜にはトラブルで帰れず、
木曜には鍋パーティの来襲を受け、
二日分の作業が停滞した。
findings.todokanai: Then on Wednesday we were tied down all day at work, and on Thursday we were forced to participate in a hot pot party,

findings.highlight: At this rate, the two of us won't be able to enjoy the weekend at our new home.
findings.evidenceJa: 多分、荷物を解くこともなく二人して倒れてるんだろうな。……月曜の朝まで。
findings.explanation: Haruki predicts something much more concrete and comic: they will collapse without even unpacking and stay down until Monday morning. The generic loss of an enjoyable weekend removes both the physical exhaustion and the setup for unpacking being postponed into New Year.
findings.japanese:
このままじゃ、せっかく新居に移って週末を過ごそうにも、
多分、荷物を解くこともなく二人して倒れてるんだろうな。
……月曜の朝まで。
findings.todokanai: At this rate, the two of us won't be able to enjoy the weekend at our new home.

findings.highlight: This is the coldest time of the year, after all.
findings.evidenceJa: だいたい今くらいが一番寒い時間帯だからな
findings.explanation: 時間帯 is a period of the day: Haruki says this pre-dawn hour is about the coldest part of the day. The translation changes that immediate observation into a claim about the season.
findings.japanese: 「だいたい今くらいが一番寒い時間帯だからな」
findings.todokanai: "This is the coldest time of the year, after all."

findings.highlight: During what is practically moments before New Year's,
findings.evidenceJa: まさに夜明け前の一瞬。
findings.explanation: The narration says it is the brief moment just before dawn, continuing the preceding line about the coldest hour. Todokanai TL mistakes 夜明け for the turn of the year and moves the scene's temporal focus from sunrise to New Year's.
findings.japanese:
まさに夜明け前の一瞬。
雲一つない空の下を、凍えるような冷気が支配していた。
findings.todokanai: During what is practically moments before New Year's, the icy cold wind dominates everything under the cloudless sky.

findings.highlight: Her hand isーas she herself puts itーlow in blood pressure
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっとだけ（自称）低血圧気味の彼女の手は、俺のより若干冷たく感じたけれど。
findings.explanation: Setsuna, self-described as tending toward low blood pressure, has a hand that feels slightly colder than Haruki's. A hand cannot itself be 'low in blood pressure'; the modifier has been attached to the wrong noun and the resulting English is nonsensical.
findings.japanese:
ちょっとだけ（自称）低血圧気味の彼女の手は、
俺のより若干冷たく感じたけれど。
findings.todokanai: Her hand isーas she herself puts itーlow in blood pressure, so it feels a decent bit colder than mine.

findings.highlight: And for Setsuna, this walkway is a path she went down nearly every day on her way to school.
findings.evidenceJa: 付属、大学の７年間、毎日のように通ったはずの道。
findings.explanation: The source specifies the full seven years of affiliated high school and university. Replacing that span with the generic 'on her way to school' erases the precise duration that makes her sudden nostalgia seem initially absurd and connects both stages of their shared history.
findings.japanese:
しかも雪菜にとって、付属、大学の７年間、
毎日のように通ったはずの道。
findings.todokanai: And for Setsuna, this walkway is a path she went down nearly every day on her way to school.

findings.highlight: That's why looking for ourselves is important, to touch…
findings.evidenceJa: だから、自分から見ること、触れることが必要
findings.explanation: 自分から means taking the initiative oneself: one has to choose to look at and touch what is nearby. 'Looking for ourselves' instead suggests self-discovery, while the stranded infinitive 'to touch' does not form intelligible English.
findings.japanese:
だから、自分から見ること、触れることが必要……
いや、何に対してそう思ったのかは置いといて。
findings.todokanai: That's why looking for ourselves is important, to touch… Let's set aside what specifically I'm referring to.

findings.highlight: nor that her department's building was right next to mine.
findings.evidenceJa: すぐ隣の、同じ大学に通っていたにも関わらず。
findings.explanation: The university itself was right next door, and both attended that same university despite Haruki fleeing this road after graduation. The source says nothing about their departments or adjacent faculty buildings; Todokanai TL invents a campus geography and changes what 'right next door' modifies.
findings.japanese: すぐ隣の、同じ大学に通っていたにも関わらず。
findings.todokanai: It didn't matter that we were in the same university, nor that her department's building was right next to mine.

findings.highlight: and the memories of her absence.
findings.evidenceJa: それ以外の、ほんの少しの思い出を
findings.explanation: Haruki sinks into memory his many recollections with Setsuna and the small number of other memories associated with the place. The Japanese deliberately leaves those other memories unnamed; defining them as memories of Setsuna's absence imposes a specific emotional interpretation not stated here.
findings.japanese:
雪菜とのたくさんの思い出と、
それ以外の、ほんの少しの思い出を……
findings.todokanai: The endless memories I share with Setsuna here, and the memories of her absence.

findings.highlight: in second grade
findings.evidenceJa: ２年の頃の雪菜って、評判の学園アイドルじゃん。
findings.explanation: This is Setsuna's second year of high school, not second grade. In English, 'second grade' places the famous school idol in elementary school and makes the ensuing Miss Houjou High history temporally absurd.
findings.japanese:
「だって２年の頃の雪菜って、評判の学園アイドルじゃん。
俺と接点ができるなんて夢にも思わないって」
findings.todokanai: "But in second grade you were the famous school idol, Setsuna. I never even imagined I'd ever get a chance to talk to you."

findings.highlight: Thinking about it now, it doesn't make any sense how a guy like you could've been popular with girls.
findings.evidenceJa: それも、わたしはともかく、あんな凄い美人に
findings.explanation: Setsuna continues by specifying the astonishingly beautiful woman who wanted Haruki, while ostentatiously setting herself aside. Todokanai TL cuts that jealous, self-flattering qualification and leaves the quotation open, so Haruki's rebuke about transparent self-deprecation loses the words that provoked it.
findings.japanese:
「今から考えても、あの頃の春希くんがモテるのって
納得いかないよね～。
それも、わたしはともかく、あんな凄い美人に」
findings.todokanai: "Thinking about it now, it doesn't make any sense how a guy like you could've been popular with girls.

findings.highlight: We walked the Houjou University grounds and the area around the main gate of the high school,
findings.evidenceJa: 学生時代の思い出を（ちょっと不穏なものも含め）語りつつ
findings.explanation: The sentence omits the action governing the walk: they talk through their student memories, including some slightly disturbing ones. That parenthetical is part of the mature couple's ability to revisit their entire past, and the translated line simply stops at a comma.
findings.japanese:
峰城大学や、付属の正門あたりを歩き、
学生時代の思い出を（ちょっと不穏なものも含め）
語りつつ……
findings.todokanai: We walked the Houjou University grounds and the area around the main gate of the high school,

findings.highlight: I lost touch with her again,
findings.evidenceJa: 愛して、迷って、愛して、揺れて、そして愛して
findings.explanation: More than half of Haruki's cumulative history is missing after the second estrangement: loving, wavering, loving, faltering, and finally loving again. The omitted crescendo is what carries the sentence from betrayal and flight to the settled love of this ending.
findings.japanese:
憧れて、結ばれたと思い込んで、裏切って、逃げて、
すれ違って、近づこうとして、またすれ違って、
愛して、迷って、愛して、揺れて、そして愛して……
findings.todokanai: I adored her, I thought she was mine, I betrayed her, I ran away from her, I lost touch with her, I tried getting closer to her, I lost touch with her again,

findings.highlight: that after her anger and lecturing, she'll forgive me.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らは俺に怒り、さんざん説教をした後、許してくれるって
findings.explanation: 彼ら is Setsuna's family collectively: Haruki now trusts that they will be angry, lecture him thoroughly, and then forgive him. Todokanai TL twice turns the plural family into a singular woman, weakening the point that he has finally learned to accept the Ogisos as a forgiving family unit.
findings.japanese:
だって多分、彼らは俺に怒り、
さんざん説教をした後、許してくれるって……
今の俺には、そう信じられるから。
findings.todokanai: Because after all this time, I've learnt to believe… that after her anger and lecturing, she'll forgive me.

findings.highlight: you insist on lecturing others, but you can't stand getting lectured yourself
findings.evidenceJa: 他人にはあんなにお節介なのに、自分がお節介されるの嫌がるもんね
findings.explanation: お節介 is Haruki's defining tendency to meddle, fuss over people, and help without being asked. Setsuna observes that he does it constantly to others but hates receiving it himself; reducing both sides to 'lecturing' discards the established character motif and misreads the family's intrusive care.
findings.japanese:
「春希くんって、他人にはあんなにお節介なのに、
自分がお節介されるの嫌がるもんね」
findings.todokanai: "Haruki-kun, you insist on lecturing others, but you can't stand getting lectured yourself, can you?"

findings.highlight: instead opting to show
findings.evidenceJa: 反発とも共感とも違う、素直な態度で受け止める。
findings.explanation: The English stops in mid-sentence. Setsuna receives words that could deny her family with an unaffected, honest attitude distinct from either resistance or agreement; that quiet mode of acceptance is never stated.
findings.japanese:
そして雪菜は、その、
自分の家族を否定されたとも取れる俺の言葉を、
反発とも共感とも違う、素直な態度で受け止める。
findings.todokanai: But Setsuna, in response to my statement that could very well be seen as a rejection of her family, neither agrees nor disagrees, instead opting to show

findings.highlight: the two had promised not to do it outside.
findings.evidenceJa: けれど外でやるなよっていう約束を交わしている。
findings.explanation: They are exchanging an ordinary, natural marital promise of the sort that makes the narrator interject, 'but don't do that outside.' Todokanai TL turns the aside into a pre-existing agreement not to perform the ceremony outdoors, directly contradicting the fact that they are doing it in a deserted park.
findings.japanese:
すごくありきたりで、とても自然で、
けれど外でやるなよっていう約束を交わしている。
findings.todokanai: It was a perfectly ordinary ceremony, and perfectly natural. However, the two had promised not to do it outside.

findings.highlight: The woman I will soon be calling "mom" in front of our child.
findings.evidenceJa: もうしばらくしたら『お母さん』って呼ぶようになる女性を
findings.explanation: The implied future subject is their baby: Haruki embraces the woman whom someone will soon call 'Mom.' Todokanai TL instead makes Haruki himself begin calling his wife 'mom' in front of the child, reversing the family relation at the emotional peak of the pregnancy revelation.
findings.japanese:
もうしばらくしたら
『お母さん』って呼ぶようになる女性を……
findings.todokanai: The woman I will soon be calling "mom" in front of our child.

findings.highlight: to the apartment where she used to…
findings.evidenceJa: 俺の、この場所での最後の日に、あの、思い出の部屋に送ってくるなんて
findings.explanation: Haruki marvels that on his last day there Kazusa sent the postcard to that particular room laden with memories. Todokanai TL trails off after 'where she used to,' never names the room as the remembered place, and supplies an unfinished relative clause with no source predicate.
findings.japanese:
俺の、この場所での最後の日に、
あの、思い出の部屋に送ってくるなんて……
findings.todokanai: And she knowingly made sure it'd arrive today, to the apartment where she used to…
